cards.body:
Token-2022 confidential transfers?
Disabled since June.

So we engineered around it.

Civitas now uses MagicBlock's
encrypted queue + a treasury PDA gate
to pay salaries in USDC, privately,
on Solana mainnet beta.

No waiting on a re-audit.

Auditors see what they should.
The public chain stays clean.

Privacy ≠ permissionless.
Privacy + policy is the harder fight.

We chose the harder fight.

Salary is the encryption target.

Row-level access controls
are pretend-privacy.

Cryptographic privacy
is the only model
that survives the phishing question.

Pay alice.sol on the 1st of every month.

This is the entire UX of payroll.

A name. An amount. A date.
USDC arrives. Sealed.

No spreadsheets.
No CSVs.
No bank routing numbers.

Solana is the only L1 where:

→ A single atomic tx encodes
   compliance + private settlement
→ Block times let payroll feel like Stripe
→ Fees stay under a cent at any scale

This is not a multi-chain pitch.
This is an L1 pitch.

Why Civitas stays Solana-only:

L2s settle on a slower layer.
Bridges are exploit surfaces.
EVM has no production
private-payment primitive.

Solana has alt_bn128.
Sub-second finality.
Sub-cent fees.
A working private rail.

We stay.

Devnet is the dress rehearsal.
Mainnet is the show.

Same program.
Same flow.
Same UX.
Same privacy guarantees.

The difference is
what's at stake on the other side
of `authorize_disburse`.

slides.headline: What if your code could prove it's the same code, every time?
slides.subhead: TEE attestation, explained without the cryptography jargon.

slides.headline: When payroll math runs on a server, you trust the server operator.
slides.body: What if you didn't have to?

slides.headline: A CPU-level secure enclave where memory is encrypted and code execution is measured.
slides.body: The CPU itself enforces it. Even the OS can't peek inside.

slides.headline: The specific TEE Nillion uses.
list: Memory encryption — RAM is ciphertext to outside code
Attestation — enclave signs proof of what's inside

slides.headline: The enclave signs a measurement of its own code.
slides.body:
You verify the signature.
You know the exact code that ran.

Not 'trust the vendor'. Math.

slides.headline: Run one long-lived enclave. Pin the measurement. Sign inputs with Ed25519.
slides.body:
~200x faster than spinning a new enclave per request.

This is the pattern Civitas uses for payroll runs.

slides.headline: Civitas runs payroll compute inside nilCC.
slides.body:
Pinned measurement. Ed25519-signed inputs. Our ops team cannot tamper with payroll math.

Period.
